proposals.before: They ran decoy coffers out each gate and hid his true burial in the hills.
proposals.after: That night they prepared more than ten coffins and sent them out through the four gates, burying him secretly in the mountain valleys; in the end, no one knew where his body lay.
proposals.reason: 棺 means coffins, not coffers; preserve the number, nocturnal setting and uncertain location. The text does not explicitly identify any particular coffin as a decoy.

proposals.before: He was posthumously titled Emperor Xianwu.
proposals.after: He was given the posthumous title Emperor Xianwu, which the Jin historian regarded as illegitimate.
proposals.reason: 偽諡 marks a posthumous title as illegitimate from the historiographer’s perspective; this formulation needs independent contextual and stylistic review.

proposals.before: His temple posthumous title was Emperor Xianwu.
proposals.after: He was given the posthumous title Emperor Xianwu, which the Jin historian regarded as illegitimate.
proposals.reason: 諡 is a posthumous title, not a temple name; 偽 expresses the historiographer’s delegitimizing judgment. Independently review its appropriate English rendering.

decisions.reason: 十餘棺 specifies over ten coffins; 夜, 分出四門, 潛葬山谷 and 竟不知其屍之所在 provide the night, four gates, concealed burial and unknown resting place. The suggested wording restores these details without inventing an identified decoy coffin.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃夜為十餘棺，分出四門，潛葬山谷，竟不知其屍之所在。

decisions.after: His posthumous title was Emperor Xianwu, a title this history treats as illegitimate.
decisions.reason: 偽 expresses the source's judgment of illegitimacy, while 諡 is a posthumous title. Avoid 'the Jin historian': the Book of Jin is a later compilation, so that label misleadingly suggests an author from the Jin period. The wording attributes the judgment to this history rather than endorsing it.

decisions.after: His posthumous title was Emperor Xianwu, a title this history treats as illegitimate.
decisions.reason: 諡 is the posthumous designation, not a temple name. 偽 expresses this history's claim of illegitimacy; the proposed 'Jin historian' risks misidentifying the compiler's period. Zizhi Tongjian 114 separately distinguishes 諡獻武皇帝 from 廟號世宗.

sourceWitness.citation: Jinshu 127, s0279, sealed dossier; compare Zizhi Tongjian 114
